title: I Benchmarked Local LLMs on the Laptop I Already Have
excerpt: Local-model benchmarks all seem to run on 128GB Macs I don't own. I ran five current open models on my 16GB M1 Pro against 21 real tasks, SQL and bug fixes and quick lookups, and priced the same work at API rates. The models did better than I expected, but the savings never showed up.
content_html:
My last post was about companies discovering their AI bills and installing caps. A reasonable reaction to that post is the one the local-LLM crowd has been giving all year: stop renting tokens, the open models are good now, just run them on your own machine.

The benchmarks backing that advice have a hardware problem. The writeups that measure anything run on Mac Studios or 128GB M5 Max laptops, and the headline stories are worse. DeepSeek V4 Flash “runs on a MacBook” if the MacBook is a 128GB build that costs about $5,000. Kimi K3 has open weights that need eight H100s just to load. One guide this summer was literally titled “Open Weights You Can’t Run.”

My laptop is a 2021 M1 Pro with 16GB of RAM. It’s almost five years old, and I suspect it’s a lot closer to the median developer machine than anything in those benchmarks. So I benchmarked what it can actually do.

The Setup⌗

I tested five models, all pulled through Ollama, all picked to fit in 16GB:

  • qwen3.5:4b and qwen3.5:9b, Alibaba’s current small models, both of which think before answering by default
  • gemma4:e4b-it-qat and gemma4:12b-it-qat, Google’s current small family, in the quantization-aware builds
  • qwen2.5:7b, a late-2024 model, as the baseline for whether a year of progress shows up at this size

The current models everyone actually talks about didn’t make the list, and that’s a finding on its own. glm-4.7-flash and qwen3-coder both sound small and both are 19GB downloads. Qwen3.8-27B, announced the week I ran this, needs about 17GB and its weights weren’t even downloadable yet, they’re promised for the week this post goes out. On 16GB of RAM the list of models you can actually run is much shorter than online discussions suggest.

The tasks are 21 problems of the kind that come up in a data engineer’s week, in six categories: writing DuckDB SQL against a seeded database, fixing buggy Python files with a failing test suite, extracting JSON from messy text like Airflow logs and billing emails, predicting what tricky Python snippets print, answering quick questions I’d normally google, and finding facts planted in a 7,400-token runbook. Everything is graded by code, not by me reading the answers: generated SQL gets executed and compared row by row against a reference query, bug fixes have to pass pytest, extractions are checked field by field. Each model also has a temperature setting that controls how much randomness goes into its answers, I set it to zero and ran everything twice, so each model gets 42 runs.

What Passed⌗

modelsizepass ratetotal wall time
gemma4:12b-it-qat7.2GB38/42 (90%)123 min
gemma4:e4b-it-qat6.1GB36/42 (86%)18 min
qwen3.5:9b6.6GB34/42 (81%)114 min
qwen3.5:4b3.4GB26/42 (62%)125 min
qwen2.5:7b4.7GB22/42 (52%)3 min

Two things surprised me here. The first is how much these models get right. Gemma 4’s 12B answered 90% of the suite correctly, including 6/6 bug fixes that had to pass an actual test suite and 8/10 SQL questions graded by execution. The 2024 baseline managed 52% on the same tasks and went 0 for 6 on predicting what Python code prints, so the models did improve over the year, at least between those two.

The second surprise is the wall-time column. The old qwen2.5 ripped through the whole suite in 3 minutes. The models that beat it needed one to two hours for the same 42 runs, and almost all of that gap is reasoning tokens.

The Reasoning Tax⌗

The current generation thinks before answering, and on a laptop that thinking is where most of the time goes.

My first run capped generation at 3,072 tokens per task, which is not much considering how many tokens something like Claude uses on a single request. The qwen3.5 models hit that cap in 48 out of 84 runs, spending the entire budget on reasoning and never producing an answer. Both scored around 40-57%. I doubled the budget to 8,192 and reran: both gained exactly ten passes. The ability was there, the models just needed thousands of extra tokens to reach the answer. Some runs blew through the doubled budget too. qwen3.5:9b spent eight minutes and 34,000 characters of thinking on one SQL question and still ran out of room.

The gemma models think too, usually less, but not always. On one run, gemma4:12b spent 14 minutes reasoning about which numeric chmod mode corresponds to rwxr-xr–, produced 19,000 characters of thinking, and answered 750. The answer is 754.

On the API this same behavior shows up as a line item, the reasoning tokens get billed like any others. Locally it shows up as time spent waiting.

Would You Stop Googling Things?⌗

The speed question I actually cared about: for a quick factual lookup, does asking a local model beat a search engine?

For the non-thinking models the answer is yes, at least on latency. With the model already loaded, “what port does Postgres use” came back in 0.6 to 1.1 seconds from gemma4:e4b and qwen2.5. That’s faster than I can type the query into a browser. The reasoning models don’t compete here: qwen3.5:9b averaged 17 seconds per quick question and the 4B averaged 38, which is slower than any search engine.

The problem is what comes back at that speed. Three models gave three different wrong answers to the chmod question: 752, 744, 750. Two models suggested git reset HEAD~ or HEAD^ for “undo the last commit but keep changes staged”, which does the opposite, plain git reset unstages. The wrong answers came back just as fast and just as confident as the right ones. A search result page gives you Stack Overflow votes and three competing answers to cross-check. A local model gives you one answer and no way to tell whether it’s right.

The Long Document Test⌗

Pasting a 7,400-token runbook and asking a question is where laptop hardware shows its actual limit. All five models found the planted facts, even the one buried near the very end, so ability isn’t the problem. The problem is the wait: 32 seconds for the first question on gemma4:e4b, 84 on qwen3.5:4b, 148 on gemma4:12b. My M1 Pro processes an incoming prompt at 130 to 330 tokens per second, and that’s why nobody runs coding agents against laptop models. A Claude Code-style harness sends tens of thousands of tokens of system prompt and context with every request. At laptop speeds that means waiting minutes before the answer even starts, on every request the agent makes.

One pleasant surprise: follow-up questions about the same document came back fast, 17 to 40 seconds, because Ollama keeps the already-processed document in memory. Chatting with one long document works locally, but anything that sends a fresh context on every request does not.

The Money⌗

Here’s the table I actually built this benchmark for. The whole suite, 210 runs, used 162,000 input tokens and 412,000 output tokens. Priced at current API rates, all of it together costs:

providerwhole benchmark
Claude Opus 5 ($5/$25 per 1M)$11.11
GPT-5.6 Terra ($2/$12)$5.27
DeepSeek V4 Flash ($0.14/$0.28)$0.14
Muse contributor tier ($0.10/$0.20)$0.10

The entire benchmark, every model, every rerun, is fourteen cents at DeepSeek’s prices, and Meta will go lower if you let them train on your prompts. Against that, my laptop spent 6.4 hours producing the local answers. The electricity rounds to a few cents, so local is technically cheaper than Opus. That stops being true the moment my time is worth anything, and at DeepSeek’s prices there is nothing to save at all. When Uber caps engineers at $1,500 a month, you cannot offload any meaningful part of that onto a machine that needs two hours to do fourteen cents of work.

So the real reason to run local models on a normal laptop isn’t money. It’s the situations where the API isn’t an option: data that can’t leave the machine, working offline, or the API being down. And I found one more reason I didn’t expect. gemma4:e4b got every extraction task in the suite right, and running it costs nothing no matter how many times I do it. That feels different from using an API where every request adds to the bill.

What I’d Actually Keep⌗

If one model earns a spot on this machine, it’s gemma4:e4b-it-qat. It passed 86% of the suite at 30 tokens per second, answers quick questions in under a second, and finished the whole benchmark in 18 minutes while the 12B needed two hours for four percentage points more. That’s enough to keep it as an offline fallback and a free JSON-extraction tool.

The rest can go. The 12B is too slow to wait for on this hardware, the reasoning models take longer than the answers are worth, and the 2024 baseline was a nice reminder of how much these small models improved in a year, 52% to 90% at roughly the same size.

So back to the advice from the top of the post. Running models locally works better than I expected on the laptop I already have. But it won’t shrink an AI bill, and the bill was the reason to try this in the first place.

blocks.html_en: The second surprise is the wall-time column. The old qwen2.5 ripped through the whole suite in 3 minutes. The models that beat it needed one to two hours for the same 42 runs, and almost all of that gap is reasoning tokens.

sentences.en: The second surprise is the wall-time column.

sentences.en: The old qwen2.5 ripped through the whole suite in 3 minutes.
sentences.zh: 旧的qwen2.5在3分钟内撕裂了整个套件。

sentences.en: The models that beat it needed one to two hours for the same 42 runs, and almost all of that gap is reasoning tokens.
sentences.zh: 击败它的模型需要一到两个小时才能完成同样的 42 次运行，而几乎所有的差距都是推理标记。

blocks.html_en: <figcaption>Accuracy against time for the whole suite. Only gemma4:e4b is both fast and accurate.</figcaption>

sentences.en: Accuracy against time for the whole suite.

sentences.zh: 只有 gemma4:e4b 既快速又准确。

sentences.en: The Reasoning Tax⌗
sentences.zh: 推理税⌗

blocks.html_en: The current generation thinks before answering, and on a laptop that thinking is where most of the time goes.

sentences.en: The current generation thinks before answering, and on a laptop that thinking is where most of the time goes.
sentences.zh: 当前这一代人在回答之前会先思考，而在笔记本电脑上，思考就是大部分时间进行的地方。

blocks.html_en: My first run capped generation at 3,072 tokens per task, which is not much considering how many tokens something like Claude uses on a single request. The qwen3.5 models hit that cap in 48 out of 84 runs, spending the entire budget on reasoning and never producing an answer. Both scored around 40-57%. I doubled the budget to 8,192 and reran: both gained exactly ten passes. The ability was there, the models just needed thousands of extra tokens to reach the answer. Some runs blew through the doubled budget too. qwen3.5:9b spent eight minutes and 34,000 characters of thinking on one SQL question and still ran out of room.

sentences.en: My first run capped generation at 3,072 tokens per task, which is not much considering how many tokens something like Claude uses on a single request.
sentences.zh: 我的第一次运行将每个任务的生成上限限制为 3,072 个令牌，考虑到像 Claude 这样的人在单个请求上使用了多少个令牌，这并不算多。

sentences.en: The qwen3.5 models hit that cap in 48 out of 84 runs, spending the entire budget on reasoning and never producing an answer.
sentences.zh: qwen3.5 模型在 84 次运行中的 48 次中达到了该上限，将全部预算都花在了推理上，却从未给出答案。

sentences.en: Both scored around 40-57%.
sentences.zh: 两者得分都在 40-57% 左右。

sentences.en: I doubled the budget to 8,192 and reran: both gained exactly ten passes.
sentences.zh: 我将预算增加了一倍，达到 8,192 并重新运行：两者都获得了 10 次通过。

sentences.en: The ability was there, the models just needed thousands of extra tokens to reach the answer.
sentences.zh: 能力就在那里，模型只需要数千个额外的标记即可得出答案。

sentences.en: Some runs blew through the doubled budget too.
sentences.zh: 有些运行也超出了双倍的预算。

sentences.en: qwen3.5:9b spent eight minutes and 34,000 characters of thinking on one SQL question and still ran out of room.
sentences.zh: qwen3.5:9b 在一个 SQL 问题上花了 8 分钟和 34,000 个字符思考，但仍然没有空间。

blocks.html_en: The gemma models think too, usually less, but not always. On one run, gemma4:12b spent 14 minutes reasoning about which numeric chmod mode corresponds to rwxr-xr–, produced 19,000 characters of thinking, and answered 750. The answer is 754.

sentences.en: The gemma models think too, usually less, but not always.
sentences.zh: Gemma 模型也会思考，通常较少，但并非总是如此。

sentences.en: On one run, gemma4:12b spent 14 minutes reasoning about which numeric chmod mode corresponds to rwxr-xr–, produced 19,000 characters of thinking, and answered 750.
sentences.zh: 在一次运行中，gemma4:12b 花了 14 分钟推理哪个数字 chmod 模式对应于 rwxr-xr–，产生了 19,000 个思考字符，并回答了 750 个。

sentences.en: The answer is 754.
sentences.zh: 答案是754。

blocks.html_en: On the API this same behavior shows up as a line item, the reasoning tokens get billed like any others. Locally it shows up as time spent waiting.

blocks.html_en: Would You Stop Googling Things?⌗

sentences.en: Would You Stop Googling Things?⌗
sentences.zh: 你会停止谷歌搜索吗？⌗

blocks.html_en: The speed question I actually cared about: for a quick factual lookup, does asking a local model beat a search engine?

sentences.en: The speed question I actually cared about: for a quick factual lookup, does asking a local model beat a search engine?
sentences.zh: 我真正关心的速度问题：对于快速的事实查找，询问本地模型是否会击败搜索引擎？

blocks.html_en: For the non-thinking models the answer is yes, at least on latency. With the model already loaded, “what port does Postgres use” came back in 0.6 to 1.1 seconds from gemma4:e4b and qwen2.5. That’s faster than I can type the query into a browser. The reasoning models don’t compete here: qwen3.5:9b averaged 17 seconds per quick question and the 4B averaged 38, which is slower than any search engine.

sentences.en: For the non-thinking models the answer is yes, at least on latency.
sentences.zh: 对于非思维模型来说，答案是肯定的，至少在延迟方面是这样。

sentences.en: With the model already loaded, “what port does Postgres use” came back in 0.6 to 1.1 seconds from gemma4:e4b and qwen2.5.
sentences.zh: 模型已经加载后，“Postgres 使用什么端口”在 0.6 到 1.1 秒内从 gemma4:e4b 和 qwen2.5 返回。

sentences.en: That’s faster than I can type the query into a browser.
sentences.zh: 这比我在浏览器中输入查询要快。

sentences.en: The reasoning models don’t compete here: qwen3.5:9b averaged 17 seconds per quick question and the 4B averaged 38, which is slower than any search engine.
sentences.zh: 推理模型在这里不竞争：qwen3.5:9b 平均每个快速问题 17 秒，4B 平均 38 秒，比任何搜索引擎都慢。

blocks.html_en: <figcaption>Median time to a quick answer with the model already loaded. The slow ones spend that time reasoning.</figcaption>

sentences.en: Median time to a quick answer with the model already loaded.

sentences.en: The slow ones spend that time reasoning.
sentences.zh: 反应迟钝的人会把时间花在推理上。

blocks.html_en: The problem is what comes back at that speed. Three models gave three different wrong answers to the chmod question: 752, 744, 750. Two models suggested git reset HEAD~ or HEAD^ for “undo the last commit but keep changes staged”, which does the opposite, plain git reset unstages. The wrong answers came back just as fast and just as confident as the right ones. A search result page gives you Stack Overflow votes and three competing answers to cross-check. A local model gives you one answer and no way to tell whether it’s right.

sentences.en: The problem is what comes back at that speed.
sentences.zh: 问题是以这样的速度返回的是什么。

sentences.en: Three models gave three different wrong answers to the chmod question: 752, 744, 750.
sentences.zh: 三个模型对 chmod 问题给出了三个不同的错误答案：752、744、750。

sentences.en: Two models suggested git reset HEAD~ or HEAD^ for “undo the last commit but keep changes staged”, which does the opposite, plain git reset unstages.
sentences.zh: 两个模型建议使用 git reset HEAD~ 或 HEAD^ 来“撤消最后一次提交，但保留暂存的更改”，这会执行相反的操作，即简单的 git reset unstages。

sentences.en: The wrong answers came back just as fast and just as confident as the right ones.
sentences.zh: 错误答案的反馈速度与正确答案一样快、一样自信。

sentences.en: A search result page gives you Stack Overflow votes and three competing answers to cross-check.
sentences.zh: 搜索结果页面为您提供 Stack Overflow 投票和三个相互竞争的答案以进行交叉检查。

sentences.zh: 本地模型只能给你一个答案，但无法判断它是否正确。

blocks.html_en: The Long Document Test⌗

sentences.en: The Long Document Test⌗
sentences.zh: 长文档测试⌗

blocks.html_en: Pasting a 7,400-token runbook and asking a question is where laptop hardware shows its actual limit. All five models found the planted facts, even the one buried near the very end, so ability isn’t the problem. The problem is the wait: 32 seconds for the first question on gemma4:e4b, 84 on qwen3.5:4b, 148 on gemma4:12b. My M1 Pro processes an incoming prompt at 130 to 330 tokens per second, and that’s why nobody runs coding agents against laptop models. A Claude Code-style harness sends tens of thousands of tokens of system prompt and context with every request. At laptop speeds that means waiting minutes before the answer even starts, on every request the agent makes.

sentences.en: Pasting a 7,400-token runbook and asking a question is where laptop hardware shows its actual limit.
sentences.zh: 粘贴 7,400 个令牌的运行手册并提出问题是笔记本电脑硬件显示其实际极限的地方。

sentences.zh: 克劳德代码风格的工具会针对每个请求发送数以万计的系统提示和上下文标记。

sentences.zh: 以笔记本电脑的速度，这意味着在回答开始之前，对于代理提出的每个请求，都要等待几分钟。

blocks.html_en: One pleasant surprise: follow-up questions about the same document came back fast, 17 to 40 seconds, because Ollama keeps the already-processed document in memory. Chatting with one long document works locally, but anything that sends a fresh context on every request does not.

sentences.en: One pleasant surprise: follow-up questions about the same document came back fast, 17 to 40 seconds, because Ollama keeps the already-processed document in memory.

sentences.zh: 与一个长文档聊天可以在本地进行，但任何在每个请求上发送新上下文的内容都行不通。

That stops being true the moment my time is worth anything, and at DeepSeek’s prices there is nothing to save at all. When Uber caps engineers at $1,500 a month, you cannot offload any meaningful part of that onto a machine that needs two hours to do fourteen cents of work.

blocks.html_en: So the real reason to run local models on a normal laptop isn’t money. It’s the situations where the API isn’t an option: data that can’t leave the machine, working offline, or the API being down. And I found one more reason I didn’t expect. gemma4:e4b got every extraction task in the suite right, and running it costs nothing no matter how many times I do it. That feels different from using an API where every request adds to the bill.

blocks.html_en: What I’d Actually Keep⌗

blocks.html_en: If one model earns a spot on this machine, it’s gemma4:e4b-it-qat. It passed 86% of the suite at 30 tokens per second, answers quick questions in under a second, and finished the whole benchmark in 18 minutes while the 12B needed two hours for four percentage points more. That’s enough to keep it as an offline fallback and a free JSON-extraction tool.

blocks.html_en: So back to the advice from the top of the post. Running models locally works better than I expected on the laptop I already have. But it won’t shrink an AI bill, and the bill was the reason to try this in the first place.

sentences.en: But it won’t shrink an AI bill, and the bill was the reason to try this in the first place.
sentences.zh: 但它不会减少人工智能的账单，而该法案是首先尝试这一点的原因。

content_html_zh:
我的上一篇文章是关于公司发现他们的人工智能账单并设置上限的。 对这篇文章的合理反应是本地法学硕士人群一整年的反应：停止租用代币，开放模型现在很好，只需在自己的机器上运行它们即可。

支持该建议的基准测试存在硬件问题。 衡量 Mac Studio 或 128GB M5 Max 笔记本电脑上运行的任何内容的文章以及头条新闻都更糟糕。 如果 MacBook 是 128GB 版本，价格约为 5,000 美元，则 DeepSeek V4 Flash“在 MacBook 上运行”。 Kimi K3 具有开放式配重，仅需要八台 H100 即可加载。 今年夏天的一份指南的标题是“你无法跑步的开放式重量”。

我的笔记本电脑是 2021 M1 Pro，内存为 16GB。 它已经有将近五年的历史了，我怀疑它比这些基准测试中的任何东西都更接近中位开发人员机器。 所以我对它的实际功能进行了基准测试。

设置⌗

我测试了五个型号，全部通过 Ollama，全部选择适合 16GB：

  • qwen3.5:4b和qwen3.5:9b，阿里巴巴目前的小模型，都是默认先思考再回答
  • gemma4:e4b-it-qat 和 gemma4:12b-it-qat，Google 目前的小家族，位于量化感知版本中
  • qwen2.5:7b，2024 年末的模型，作为一年的进展是否以这种规模出现的基线

每个人实际上谈论的当前模型并未出现在列表中，这本身就是一个发现。 glm-4.7-flash 和 qwen3-coder 听起来都很小，而且都是 19GB 下载。 Qwen3.8-27B，在我运行这个的那周宣布，需要大约 17GB，它的权重甚至还不能下载，他们承诺在这篇文章发布的那周。 在 16GB RAM 上，您实际可以运行的模型列表比在线讨论建议的要短得多。

这些任务是数据工程师一周中会遇到的 21 个问题，分为六类：针对种子数据库编写 DuckDB SQL、使用失败的测试套件修复有问题的 Python 文件、从 Airflow 日志和计费电子邮件等杂乱文本中提取 JSON、预测打印哪些棘手的 Python 片段、回答我通常会在 google 上搜索的快速问题，以及查找包含 7,400 个令牌的运行手册中的事实。 一切都是由代码评分，而不是由我阅读答案：生成的 SQL 被执行并与参考查询逐行进行比较，错误修复必须通过 pytest，提取是逐字段检查的。 每个模型还有一个温度设置，用于控制其答案的随机性，我将其设置为零并运行所有内容两次，因此每个模型都会运行 42 次。

qwen3.5:4b3.4GB26/42 (62%)125 min
qwen2.5:7b4.7GB22/42 (52%)3 min

这里有两件事让我感到惊讶。 首先是这些模型的正确程度。 Gemma 4 的 12B 正确回答了套件中 90% 的问题，包括必须通过实际测试套件的 6/6 个错误修复和按执行评分的 8/10 个 SQL 问题。 2024 年的基准在相同任务上成功了 52%，在预测 Python 代码打印内容方面，6 分的成绩为 0，因此这些模型在这一年中确实有所改进，至少在这两者之间是这样。

第二个惊喜是墙上的时间专栏。 旧的qwen2.5在3分钟内撕裂了整个套件。 击败它的模型需要一到两个小时才能完成同样的 42 次运行，而几乎所有的差距都是推理标记。

推理税⌗

当前这一代人在回答之前会先思考，而在笔记本电脑上，思考就是大部分时间进行的地方。

我的第一次运行将每个任务的生成上限限制为 3,072 个令牌，考虑到像 Claude 这样的人在单个请求上使用了多少个令牌，这并不算多。 qwen3.5 模型在 84 次运行中的 48 次中达到了该上限，将全部预算都花在了推理上，却从未给出答案。 两者得分都在 40-57% 左右。 我将预算增加了一倍，达到 8,192 并重新运行：两者都获得了 10 次通过。 能力就在那里，模型只需要数千个额外的标记即可得出答案。 有些运行也超出了双倍的预算。 qwen3.5:9b 在一个 SQL 问题上花了 8 分钟和 34,000 个字符思考，但仍然没有空间。

Gemma 模型也会思考，通常较少，但并非总是如此。 在一次运行中，gemma4:12b 花了 14 分钟推理哪个数字 chmod 模式对应于 rwxr-xr–，产生了 19,000 个思考字符，并回答了 750 个。 答案是754。

在 API 上，相同的行为显示为行项目，推理令牌与其他任何令牌一样计费。 在本地，它显示为等待时间。

你会停止谷歌搜索吗？⌗

我真正关心的速度问题：对于快速的事实查找，询问本地模型是否会击败搜索引擎？

对于非思维模型来说，答案是肯定的，至少在延迟方面是这样。 模型已经加载后，“Postgres 使用什么端口”在 0.6 到 1.1 秒内从 gemma4:e4b 和 qwen2.5 返回。 这比我在浏览器中输入查询要快。 推理模型在这里不竞争：qwen3.5:9b 平均每个快速问题 17 秒，4B 平均 38 秒，比任何搜索引擎都慢。

问题是以这样的速度返回的是什么。 三个模型对 chmod 问题给出了三个不同的错误答案：752、744、750。 两个模型建议使用 git reset HEAD~ 或 HEAD^ 来“撤消最后一次提交，但保留暂存的更改”，这会执行相反的操作，即简单的 git reset unstages。 错误答案的反馈速度与正确答案一样快、一样自信。 搜索结果页面为您提供 Stack Overflow 投票和三个相互竞争的答案以进行交叉检查。 本地模型只能给你一个答案，但无法判断它是否正确。

长文档测试⌗

粘贴 7,400 个令牌的运行手册并提出问题是笔记本电脑硬件显示其实际极限的地方。 所有五个模型都发现了植入的事实，甚至是在最后埋藏的事实，所以能力不是问题。 问题是等待：在 gemma4:e4b 上第一个问题等待 32 秒，在 qwen3.5:4b 上等待 84 秒，在 gemma4:12b 上等待 148 秒。 我的 M1 Pro 以每秒 130 到 330 个令牌的速度处理传入提示，这就是为什么没有人针对笔记本电脑型号运行编码代理。 克劳德代码风格的工具会针对每个请求发送数以万计的系统提示和上下文标记。 以笔记本电脑的速度，这意味着在回答开始之前，对于代理提出的每个请求，都要等待几分钟。

令人惊喜的是：有关同一文档的后续问题很快就会返回，只需 17 到 40 秒，因为 Ollama 将已处理的文档保留在内存中。 与一个长文档聊天可以在本地进行，但任何在每个请求上发送新上下文的内容都行不通。

钱⌗

这是我实际构建此基准的表格。 整个套件运行了 210 次，使用了 162,000 个输入令牌和 412,000 个输出令牌。 按当前 API 价格定价，所有费用合计：

提供者整体基准
关闭 Opus 5（每 100 万 5 美元/25 美元）$11.11
GPT-5.6 Terra（2 美元/12 美元）$5.27
DeepSeek V4 闪存（0.14 美元/0.28 美元）$0.14
Muse 贡献者等级 ($0.10/$0.20)$0.10

整个基准测试、每个模型、每次重新运行，按 DeepSeek 的价格计算是 14 美分，如果你让他们按照你的提示进行训练，Meta 的价格会更低。 相比之下，我的笔记本电脑花了 6.4 小时生成本地答案。 电费四舍五入为几美分，因此从技术上讲，本地电比 Opus 便宜。 一旦我的时间变得有价值，而且按照 DeepSeek 的价格，根本就没有什么可以节省的了，这种情况就不再是真的了。 当 Uber 将工程师的工资上限定为每月 1,500 美元时，你就无法将其中任何有意义的部分转移到一台需要两个小时才能完成 14 美分工作的机器上。

因此，在普通笔记本电脑上运行本地模型的真正原因不是钱。 在这种情况下，API 不可行：数据无法离开机器、离线工作或 API 关闭。 我又发现了一个我没想到的原因。 gemma4:e4b 正确地完成了套件中的每个提取任务，并且无论我执行多少次，运行它都不需要任何成本。 这与使用 API 的感觉不同，在 API 中，每个请求都会增加账单。

我实际上会保留什么⌗

如果有一个模型在这台机器上赢得了一席之地，那就是 gemma4:e4b-it-qat。 它以每秒 30 个令牌的速度通过了套件中 86% 的测试，在一秒内回答了快速问题，并在 18 分钟内完成了整个基准测试，而 12B 需要两个小时，多了四个百分点。 这足以让它作为离线后备和免费的 JSON 提取工具。

剩下的就可以走了。 在这种硬件上，12B 的速度太慢，无法等待，推理模型花费的时间比答案的价值要长，2024 年的基线很好地提醒了我们这些小型模型在一年内改进了多少，在大致相同的大小下提高了 52% 到 90%。

那么回到帖子顶部的建议。 在我已有的笔记本电脑上本地运行模型的效果比我预期的要好。 但它不会减少人工智能的账单，而该法案是首先尝试这一点的原因。
